title: NextGen Onboarding, Skills Badging, and Benefits Playbook
author: Aisha Gomez
content:
Overview

Purpose: This playbook describes Redwood’s NextGen onboarding program that combines rapid role activation with a skills badging system and an aligned benefits matrix. The goal is to reduce time-to-impact for new contributors, provide transparent career scaffolding, and make internal tooling access predictable and measurable.

Scope

- Applies to all full-time employees, contractors, and apprentices joining engineering, product, and platform teams.
- Covers pre-boarding, first 90 days, continuous skill elevation, and benefits alignment tied to career band progression.

Objectives

1. Standardize onboarding flows so 90% of role-critical tooling is available within 72 hours of start date.
2. Ensure every contributor has a documented 30/60/90 plan and at least one mentor micro-rotation scheduled in their first 60 days.
3. Launch and maintain a skills badging catalog to objectively measure competency and to unlock role-aligned benefits.
4. Provide a single internal-tooling self-service path with SLAs and escalation steps.

High-level Timeline

- Pre-boarding (Day -14 to Day 0): account creation, equipment provisioning, role welcome packet.
- Early Ramp (Day 0–30): team orientation, base training, first contribution checklist.
- Contribution Growth (Day 30–90): competency assessments, badge applications, first 90-day review.
- Ongoing (Post-90): quarterly skill refresh, rotational opportunities, benefits alignment checkpoints.

Roles & Responsibilities

- People Ops (owner): manages central playbook, coordinates equipment & access SLAs, maintains badging catalog.
- Hiring Manager: owns 30/60/90 plan, assigns mentor, approves badge-level applications for the role.
- IT/Infrastructure: provisions devices and core accounts within SLA and tags accounts with provisioning metadata.
- Team Buddy/Mentor: supports culture, schedules micro-rotation, verifies practical competency evidence.
- New Contributor: completes onboarding tasks, applies for badges, provides feedback to People Ops.

Access & SLA Matrix

| Asset | Provisioning Owner | Target SLA |
|---|---:|---:|
| GitHub org + repo access | IT / Eng Tools | 24 hours |
| Slack workspace & team channels | People Ops | 8 hours |
| Cloud console IAM (read) | Cloud Infra | 48 hours |
| CI pipeline role (developer) | DevOps | 72 hours |
| Internal dashboards (cost, alerts) | Observability Team | 72 hours |
| Workstation (mac/linux image) | IT Hardware | 5 business days |

Tooling Self-Service Flow (summary)

1. New contributor receives a unique provisioning link from People Ops (sent at -7 days).
2. Submit device and account preferences via the onboarding form.
3. IT issues device ticket; Eng Tools creates GitHub/CI tickets; Cloud Infra creates IAM role.
4. Automated check-in email at Day 1, Day 7, Day 30.
5. If any SLA is missed: escalate to People Ops -> Hiring Manager -> Eng Tools lead.

Pre-boarding Checklist (starter)

- Confirm offer acceptance and start date.
- Send welcome packet (company values, org chart, code of conduct).
- Invite to Slack, calendar, and benefits enrollment system.
- Request hardware preferences and shipping.
- Create onboarding issues in the team board and assign buddy.

30/60/90 Playbook (for Hiring Managers)

Day 0–30 (Expectations):
- Introductions, role context, first small contribution (bugfix or doc change), complete required security training.
- Schedule a 1:1 weekly cadence and a mentor micro-rotation.

Day 30–60 (Expectations):
- Deliver a scoped task from product/roadmap; apply for Level 1 skills badges as appropriate.
- Host a knowledge-sharing session.

Day 60–90 (Expectations):
- Demonstrate ownership of a component or workflow and pass the competency evidence checklist for Level 1/2 badges.
- Performance check-in and career conversation; agree next quarter learning objectives.

Skills Badging Program

Overview: The Skills Badging Program is a lightweight credential system used to certify practical competencies. Badges are assigned by reviewers (peers or managers) based on evidence: PRs, incident participation, design docs, and live demos. Badges unlock benefit tiers and access to rotational programs.

Badge Levels & Examples:
- Foundation (Level 1): basic competency—examples: repo navigation, running local dev environment, unit testing.
- Practitioner (Level 2): independent delivery—examples: owning a feature, writing an integration test, observability dashboards.
- Specialist (Level 3): recognized domain expertise—examples: kernel of an infra system, leading model-onboarding, quantization tuning.

Badge Application & Review Process:
1. Contributor submits application with evidence links using the internal badge form.
2. Assigned reviewer (manager + peer) verifies artifacts within 7 business days.
3. Badge is awarded and recorded in HRIS and the contributor profile.

Benefits Alignment Matrix (excerpt)

| Badge Level | Typical Career Band | Benefit Unlocks |
|---|---:|---|
| Foundation (L1) | IC1–IC2 | Standard benefits + WFH stipend |
| Practitioner (L2) | IC2–IC3 | Enhanced learning budget ($2,500/yr), mentor hours allocation |
| Specialist (L3) | IC3+ / Senior Manager | Leadership stipends, conference budget, early access to dedicated capacity trials |

Hybrid Work & Ergonomics Support

- Redwood supports hybrid schedules; flexible core hours are 10:00–16:00 local.
- Ergonomics: employees qualifying for equipment allowances can order desk setup items via internal procurement form. Approval SLA: 5 business days.
- Satellite office access: provisioned by Facilities; require completed safety acknowledgment in the first 14 days.

Mentor Micro-Rotation Framework

Purpose: accelerate onboarding by exposing new contributors to adjacent systems and stakeholders.
- Duration: 2–4 days across weeks 2–8.
- Topics: release process, incident response, observability, model-onboarding walkthrough.
- Outcome: one verified artifact (example: a runbook edit, a small integration change) and a short write-up.

Onboarding Templates and Examples

- 30/60/90 template (to paste into PR):
"""
# 30/60/90 Plan
- Goals (30): 
- Goals (60):
- Goals (90):
- Mentor assigned: Name
- Key repos and dashboards: links
"""

- Badge evidence example (markdown):
"""
## Badge application: Observability Practitioner
- PR: https://github.com/redwood/example/pull/123
- Demo video: link
- Notes: Owned dashboard for X, reduced alert noise by 40%.
"""

Operational Runbook: Missed SLA Escalation (short)

1. If >72 hours for core cloud IAM: People Ops files priority ticket with Cloud Infra and assigns owner in the ticket.
2. Day 4: Hiring Manager notifies director and creates an interim access workaround (audit-logged).
3. Day 7: Exec notification and retro scheduled; permanent process fix identified.

Metrics & Reporting

- Target: 90% of new contributors reach Foundation badges within 90 days.
- Reporting cadence: People Ops publishes monthly onboarding health dashboard with: provisioning SLA attainment, badge completion rate, average time to first deploy, and feedback NPS.

Feedback Loops & Continuous Improvement

- New hire NPS survey at Day 7 and Day 90.
- Quarterly retro with Hiring Managers and Eng Tools to tune SLA and access flows.
- People Ops owns a backlog for tooling improvements and publishes an update each release cycle.

Frequently Asked Questions (selected)

Q: What if my badge review takes longer than 7 days?
A: Escalate to your hiring manager and People Ops will reassign or add an extra reviewer. Badges should not gate critical benefits if the review is delayed—use interim manager sign-off.

Q: Can I request role-specific training credits?
A: Yes. Practitioner and Specialist badge holders can request training up to the allocated learning budget; requests use the normal learning reimbursement workflow.
